title: Connecting Generations Through Energy Education
body_markdown:
For 100 years, Reddy Kilowatt has helped people understand the electricity that powers everyday life. Today, Reddy continues his legacy as Xcel Energy’s energy ambassador, helping make energy education and safety approachable for a new generation. This year marks his 100th birthday and a century as a familiar face in the utility industry.


Reddy Kilowatt was created in 1926 by Ashton B. Collins Sr. of Alabama Power Company. When electricity was still new to many Americans, Collins envisioned a character who could help people understand and embrace the technology. By giving electricity a friendly, approachable face, Reddy helped make a powerful and unfamiliar innovation feel safer, more useful and more accessible.


With his lightning bolt body, light bulb nose and electrical outlet ears, Reddy quickly became one of the most recognizable symbols in the utility industry. Over the decades, he appeared in school safety programs, educational comic books, animated films and promotional materials, helping people learn how electricity works and why using it safely matters.


In 1998, Northern States Power Company acquired Reddy Kilowatt and his trademark. Two years later, Northern States Power Company merged with New Century Energies to form Xcel Energy, bringing Reddy along with it.


Today, Reddy continues to serve as an ambassador for energy education and safety, particularly for young people and children. Through educational materials and community engagement, Reddy helps young learners understand energy, how it works and how to use it safely and responsibly. While the energy industry has changed significantly over the past century, Reddy's purpose remains rooted in making important energy concepts approachable for a new generation.


After 100 years, Reddy Kilowatt remains an iconic figure in the utility industry and an enduring part of Xcel Energy's history. His story reflects the evolution of electricity, the energy industry and the ways utilities have communicated about energy over the past century. As we celebrate this milestone, we look ahead to the next generation of learners and the many ways Reddy will continue to spark curiosity, support energy education and help make energy work better for future generations.
